solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seek a man out who may be confused with another?

definitions.text: who may be confused with another?

indicators.note: out here means wrong or misplaced, so these letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A search for a particular man who keeps getting mistaken for somebody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'seek out', but it is the anagram signal working on SEEKAMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people sharing one name are easily mixed up, so a person called the same as you may be mistaken for you.

clue.text: Advise if Tony is spinning

indicators.note: something spinning is whirled about, so the letters of the two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wants to tell Tony something, but he is dizzily turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise someone of a fact is to inform them formally, a close synonym.

clue.text: Extra large mushroom

parts.note: extra means more, as in 'some extra rice'
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An extra-large mushroom, the kind a forager boasts about.
explanation.definitionFit: The morel is an edible fungus with a honeycombed cap, an example of the wider class.

clue.text: Disease suffered primarily by heartless taxi drivers

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of suffered is used
heartless means losing the heart, so the central letter of the drivers' word is dropped

parts.note: cabbies are taxi drivers

explanation.surface: An illness supposedly suffered most of all by unkind cab drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like a slur on the drivers; it removes the middle B of CABBIES, leaving CABIES.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a contagious skin complaint caused by mites, so it is one example of an illness.

clue.text: Curiously I'd oil peacocks giving wonderful colour effects

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters of the three words are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A strange admission: someone would oil peacocks, perhaps to make their plumage shimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from the toy tube of mirrors and beads that shows ever-changing bright patterns.

clue.text: How to make quotable list for Shakespeare role

parts.note: banning the letters Q, U and O from the word quotable leaves table, which means a list

explanation.surface: Advice on drawing up a list of quotable lines from a Shakespeare part.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction, BAN QUO: strike QUO out of QUOTABLE and TABLE remains, and a table is a list.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the general in Macbeth whose ghost appears at the feast, a character from the play.

clue.text: Country regularly involved in an Ionian-Balkan uprising?

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads from bottom to top, so the picked letters are read backwards
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the phrase is taken, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A Balkan country caught up in an insurrection along the Ionian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters give AINABLA; 'uprising' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Balkan state on the Adriatic and Ionian seas, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Question a long-term prisoner about one person becoming fit?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the prisoner's word goes round the letter for one

parts.note: a lifer is someone serving a life sentence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Interrogating a lifer about someone who is getting into shape in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' suggests physical fitness, but here it means eligible, as an entrant who earns a place in a later round.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who earns a place in the next stage becomes eligible for it, so fit here means suitable.

clue.text: European motored about — this could prove it

definitions.text: European motored about — this could prove it

indicators.note: about here means around in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A European drove around, and the dashboard instrument could show that he did.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the instrument records miles driven, proving the motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashboard gauge records the distance a vehicle has travelled, evidence of how far it was driven.

clue.text: Sailor finds girl endlessly old hat

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Pauline is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sailor discovers that a girl's look is endlessly outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like the idiom for stale, but it is literal: a sailor's tarred hat of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically sailors wore a hat of tarred cloth, which took the name of the waterproof canvas.

clue.text: Trivial American — a bit more than a bit?

definitions.meaning: trivial means petty or small-time, the American sense of the phrase

definitions.text: American — a bit more than a bit?
definitions.meaning: two US coins, five cents and ten cents, add up to fifteen cents, slightly more than a bit, an old name for twelve and a half cents

explanation.surface: An unimportant American who is a little more than a little.
explanation.walkthrough: In American slang a bit is 12.5 cents (two bits make a quarter), so 15 cents in coins is a bit more than a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something petty or small-scale, like dealing only in small change.

clue.text: Supporter very obviously just started cheer

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: something just started shows only its beginning, so only the first letter of obviously is used

explanation.surface: A fan, clearly new to it, has only just begun shouting encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the shout of approval an audience gives a performer, a word of cheering.

clue.text: Joined a military formation with one film director

parts.note: soldiers fall in when they take their places in ranks, past tense fell in
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier lined up on parade alongside a cinema director.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the Italian maker of La Dolce Vita and 8½, a famous movie director.

clue.text: Restrict prisoner very well

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
fine means very well, as in 'I'm fine'

explanation.surface: An instruction to limit a convict's movements, very good.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict someone is to keep them within limits, a synonym of shutting them in.

clue.text: After theatre job, work at ENO, say, with a lot of musical backing?

parts.note: a post is a job
ENO is the English National Opera, so a work there is an opera

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the shortened musical is read in reverse
a lot of means most but not all, so the musical loses its last letter

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: An evening at the theatre, then a job working at the opera with music behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims EVITA to EVIT and 'backing' turns it into TIVE. 'theatre' means the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: It describes care following surgery, and surgery happens in an operating theatre.

clue.text: One in court with simple argument

parts.note: plain means simple
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: A litigant arrives at court with a straightforward case.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who brings a civil lawsuit appears as a party in the courtroom.

clue.text: Mounted demo one hour shortened as a result of cold?

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going upwards, so the pieces read from the bottom up

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest demonstration
I is the Roman numeral for one
HR is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: A mounted protest lasted just under an hour, perhaps because of the chilly weather.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflammation of the nasal lining is what a common cold brings on, hence the query.

clue.text: What takes warmth out of screwy Gen X heartache

indicators.note: screwy means crazy or twisted, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that drains the warmth from the unhinged heartbreak of Generation X.
explanation.definitionFit: This device moves heat from one fluid to another, so it draws warmth from a hot stream.

clue.text: Clipping a run, getting caught before time

indicators.note: before means coming earlier, so the letter for caught comes ahead of the letter for time

parts.note: in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricket highlight clip: an extra run, then a catch just before the close.
explanation.walkthrough: An extra is a run conceded by the fielding side (a wide or a no-ball), not hit off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper cutting is an excerpt taken from a larger text, as is a passage quoted out.

clue.text: See you bargain soundly

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the phrase is said aloud and spelt as a word with the same sound

parts.note: a bargain is a good buy

explanation.surface: Someone parts from a shopper who struck a very solid deal.
explanation.definitionFit: 'See you' is a casual farewell, said on parting just like the more formal word.

clue.text: For example, Dorothy's served up filling food

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
Dot is short for Dorothy, so Dorothy's gives Dot's

explanation.surface: Dorothy dishes up a hearty meal, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, starchy food such as suet pudding fills the stomach; the word means just that.

clue.text: No bridge partners lead all the time

parts.note: in bridge, North and South play as partners
to top a table is to lead it

explanation.surface: Bridge partners who are never ahead at any point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something continuous goes on without pause, without stopping at any moment.

clue.text: Doctor allowed to conceal operation tear

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the two outer pieces wrap around the operation

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A doctor permitted to hide an operation's rip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' as in rip suits the surgical surface; it is a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear from the eye is a small drop of liquid, a single bead of fluid.

clue.text: Brad brought up a climber

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means raised so the word reads upward, from the bottom

parts.note: a brad is a thin nail

explanation.surface: Brad was raised as a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brad' looks like a man's name, but it is a small nail.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical vine climbs up trees in the rainforest, so it is a climbing plant.

clue.text: Name area outside India's northern region

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the two pieces sit around the India letter

parts.note: to tag is to label or name
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pick a stretch of land outside the northern part of India.
explanation.definitionFit: This subarctic coniferous forest belt spans Siberia and Canada, a far-north zone.

clue.text: Magazine panel used in cut-and-paste operation

parts.note: a clip is a magazine of cartridges for a gun
a board is a panel, of wood or of people

explanation.surface: A magazine's editorial board involved in a collage of cuttings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests a publication, but it is the cartridge holder of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer, copied text is held in this temporary store until it is pasted elsewhere.

clue.text: Note with iron put in farm structure for protection

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the note and iron go into the pigpen

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen on a farm
A is a musical note
FE is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Iron bars fitted into a pigsty to keep the animals secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept from harm or danger is the state of being shielded, a synonym.

clue.text: Authorise English member to cut meeting

indicators.note: to cut into means to break in, so the two pieces go inside the meeting

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Permission for an English committee member to skip the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a committee member but is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a task to someone is to empower them to act on your behalf.
